recentItems.title: Hundreds of POWs and panic: third phase of offensive COLLAPSES Russian front in Donbas
recentItems.description:
In this new episode of News Pulse: reports on a strike against a vessel bound for a Russian port, attacks on Russian oil logistics, and Kremlin attempts to conceal data on the fuel crisis. We cover the Russian strike on the National Academy of Sciences building in Kyiv, as well as testing of Ukrainian interceptor drones and ground robots. On the front lines, the 3rd Army Corps summarizes the results of Operation "Vivaldi": liberated settlements, captured Russian soldiers, and robotic APCs. Also featured: Canadian aid for survivors of captivity and occupation, and the potential for a new wave of mobilization in Russia.

recentItems.title: Oleshky concentration camp: How the Russians turned a modern city into an occupied hell
recentItems.description:
Oleshky, located on the left bank of the Kherson region, lives under occupation, amidst mines and the constant threat of drones. In this teaser for the upcoming documentary film, people speak about the violence of the Russian military, the loss of loved ones, and life without electricity, water, communications, or medical assistance. Mined roads complicate food deliveries and the evacuation of the wounded. These are personal testimonies about those who still remain in Oleshky and the dangerous path to safety.

The full movie will be released very soon – don’t miss it!

recentItems.title: IS "AKHMAT" BEING LIQUIDATED? Kadyrov’s TikTok troops stripped of elite status
recentItems.description:
Ukraine is finalizing tests of its domestic FP-7 and FP-9 ballistic missiles, capable of striking targets up to 850 km away. In this new episode, we break down the prospects of Ukrainian ballistics, the aftermath of the Russian strike on Kyiv, the situation on the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Lyman fronts, the details of Operation Vivaldi, and the actions of Azov fighters. We also discuss Russia’s surging production of jet-powered Shahed drones, Ukrainian interceptor drones, and structural changes surrounding the Akhmat unit.

recentItems.title: From "Kyiv in 3 days" to crying over warehouses: The Kremlin devises an absurd excuse for terror
recentItems.description:
The Kremlin is once again searching for excuses to prolong the war, accusing Ukraine of escalation and framing its own strikes as "retaliation." In this episode, we break down why this narrative fails the chronology test, whether a mutual energy truce is possible, and why Moscow has so far refused to agree to it. Zelenskyy points to Russian plans for arms production heading into 2027 and ongoing attacks on Ukrainian data centers. Following a meeting with Lavrov, Germany's Foreign Minister similarly saw no readiness from the Russian side for constructive negotiations. What signals indicate preparations for further escalation, and what should Ukraine expect this winter? Find out more in the new episode.
